questions.question: Name the life-threatening disease caused by protozoa of the genus Trypanosoma that is transmitted to human hosts through the bite of infected tsetse flies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sleeping sickness**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sleeping sickness**, also known as **African trypanosomiasis**, is caused by **protozoa of the genus Trypanosoma**.
 
• It is transmitted to human hosts through the **bite of infected tsetse flies**, which are found in sub-Saharan Africa.
 
• The disease is characterized by two stages: the first stage involves fever, headaches, joint pains, and itching, while the second stage affects the central nervous system, leading to neurological symptoms such as confusion, sensory disturbances, and poor coordination.
 
• Without treatment, sleeping sickness can be fatal, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and intervention.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chagas disease** is another illness caused by a different species of Trypanosoma, but it is **transmitted by triatomine bugs** and is primarily found in Latin America.
 
• **Giardiasis** is a diarrheal disease **caused by the protozoan parasite Giardia**, transmitted through contaminated water or food.
 
• **Kala-azar**, also known as visceral leishmaniasis, is **caused by Leishmania parasites** and transmitted by sandfly bites.
 
• Proper vector control, public health measures, and access to medical treatment are crucial in managing and preventing the spread of these diseases.

questions.question: The black soil area of the ________ is known as the Deccan Trap.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Peninsular Plateau**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **black soil **area of the **Peninsular Plateau** is known as the **Deccan Trap**.
 
• The Deccan Trap is a large igneous province located in west-central India, known for its fertile black soil, which is ideal for **cotton cultivation**.
 
• Black soil, also known as **regur soil**, is rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime but poor in nitrogen and organic matter.
 
• It is well-known for its moisture-retentive properties, making it suitable for dry farming.
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is one of the oldest and most stable landmasses in India, composed primarily of igneous and metamorphic rocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Deccan Trap region was formed by volcanic activity that occurred between 60 and 68 million years ago during the late Cretaceous period.
 
• It covers an area of about 500,000 square kilometers, extending over several states including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and parts of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The term "Trap" is derived from the Swedish word "trappa," meaning stair, which refers to the step-like hills forming the landscape of the region.
 
• The Deccan Plateau is bounded by the Western Ghats on the west, the Eastern Ghats on the east, and the Satpura and Vindhya ranges to the north.
 
• This region plays a crucial role in India's agriculture, especially in the cultivation of cotton, soybeans, and other cash crops.

questions.question: When did the British East India Company start the ‘permanent settlement system’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1793 CE**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The British East India Company started the **'permanent settlement system' in 1793 CE**.
 
• This system was introduced by **Lord Cornwallis**.
 
• Under this system, the land revenue was fixed permanently, which means it would not be increased in the future.
 
• The zamindars were recognized as the owners of the land, and they had to pay a fixed amount of revenue to the company.
 
• This system aimed to create a loyal and wealthy class of landlords who would support British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Cornwallis was the **Governor-General of India** from **1786 to 1793**.
 
• The Permanent Settlement covered the provinces of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
• While the system aimed at revenue stability, it also led to the exploitation of peasants as zamindars often demanded high rents.
 
• The system had long-term impacts on the agrarian structure and revenue collection in India.

• **Gujarat** is not included in the list of the 10 poorest states according to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022.

questions.question: Which Clause of Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the ‘right to move freely throughout the territory of India’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clause (d)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Clause (d)** of Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the 'right to move freely throughout the territory of India'.
 
• Article 19 of the Indian Constitution provides citizens with certain fundamental rights, including the right to freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• The right to move freely ensures that citizens can travel, reside, and settle in any part of India without any restrictions, promoting national integration and unity.
 
• This right is subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of the general public or for the protection of the interests of any Scheduled Tribe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• Article 19 is part of the fundamental rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, which provides citizens with essential freedoms and rights.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, ensuring that the government does not infringe upon the fundamental liberties of individuals.

questions.question: What is the main function of money in an economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To facilitate exchange**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To facilitate exchange** is the main function of money in an economy.
 
• Money serves as a **medium of exchange**, allowing goods and services to be traded without the complications of a barter system.
 
• It acts as a **store of value**, enabling individuals to save and defer consumption until a later date.
 
• Money also functions as a **unit of account**, providing a common measure for valuing goods and services.
 
• Additionally, it serves as a **standard of deferred payment**, facilitating transactions over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interest rates** are typically regulated by central banks and are not the primary function of money itself.
 
• **Creating wealth** is a result of economic activities and investments, not a direct function of money.
 
• **Controlling inflation** is a monetary policy goal achieved through various tools, including money supply management, but it is not a direct function of money.
 
• The concept of money has evolved over time, from commodity money (like gold and silver) to fiat money (government-issued currency), and now includes digital and cryptocurrencies.
 
• In modern economies, money is crucial for the smooth functioning of markets and the overall economy.

questions.question: Who among the following designed the India Gate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Edwin Lutyens**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Edwin Lutyens** is the architect who **designed the India Gate**.
 
• India Gate is a war memorial located astride the Rajpath, on the eastern edge of the 'ceremonial axis' of New Delhi, formerly called Kingsway.
 
• It commemorates the 70,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army who died in the First World War between 1914 and 1921.
 
• The foundation stone of India Gate was laid by His Royal Highness, the Duke of Connaught in 1921 and it was designed by Edwin Lutyens.
 
• The **structure was completed in 1931** and is a prominent landmark of Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edwin Lutyens** was a renowned British architect, known for his imaginative adaptation of traditional architectural styles to the requirements of his era.
 
• He played a significant role in designing and building New Delhi, the new capital of India under British rule.
 
• In addition to India Gate, Lutyens also designed the Rashtrapati Bhavan (formerly known as the Viceroy's House), which is the official residence of the President of India.
 
• His work in New Delhi is considered one of the crowning achievements of his career.

questions.question: In 2022, the Centre constituted a committee headed by former Union Agriculture Secretary _______ to look into the issues of minimum support price (MSP).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanjay Agrawal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2022, the Centre constituted a committee headed by former Union Agriculture Secretary **Sanjay Agrawal** to look into the issues of **minimum support price **(MSP).
 
• The committee was formed to address various concerns related to the MSP system, which is a crucial aspect of Indian agricultural policy.
 
• The MSP system ensures that farmers receive a minimum price for their produce, protecting them from price fluctuations in the market.
 
• Sanjay Agrawal's leadership in the committee is expected to bring in-depth expertise and experience in agricultural policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The formation of the committee followed widespread protests by farmers demanding better MSP and other reforms in the agricultural sector.
 
• The committee's recommendations are expected to play a significant role in shaping future agricultural policies in India.
 
• The MSP is announced by the Government of India at the beginning of the sowing season for certain crops based on the recommendations of the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)**.
 
• The aim of MSP is to **ensure remunerative prices to the growers for their produce**, thereby safeguarding the interests of the farmers.

questions.question: One of the prominent festivals celebrated in ____________ is the ‘Me-Dum-Me-Phi’, i.e., the ancestor worship festival.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Me-Dum-Me-Phi** is a significant festival celebrated in **Assam**.
 
• This festival is dedicated to **ancestor worship** and is a crucial part of the cultural heritage of the Assamese people.
 
• It is celebrated on **31st January** every year and involves various rituals and community gatherings.
 
• The festival reflects the deep-rooted respect and reverence the Assamese people have for their ancestors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Me-Dum-Me-Phi** is organized by the **Ahom community**, who were the ruling dynasty in Assam for nearly 600 years.
 
• The festival includes rituals such as **lighting lamps, offering food, and reciting hymns** in honor of the ancestors.
 
• It also serves as an occasion for community bonding and **strengthening social ties**.
 
• The festival is a reminder of the rich cultural traditions and historical legacy of the Assamese people.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of revenue expenditure in a government budget?

options.text: Payment of salary of government employees

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payment of salary of government employees**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Payment of salary of government employees** is classified as a **revenue expenditure **in a government budget.
 
• Revenue expenditure refers to the **expenses that are incurred for the normal functioning of government** departments and various services, interest payments on debt, subsidies, etc.
 
• Such expenditures do not result in the creation of assets or reduction in liabilities.
 
• Examples include **salaries, pensions, interest payments, and administrative expenses**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital expenditure**, on the other hand, includes **expenses incurred on the acquisition of assets** like land, buildings, machinery, etc., and investments in shares.
 
• It also includes loans granted by the government to states, union territories, and other parties.
 
• Examples of capital expenditure are construction of new highways, investment in state-owned companies, and repayment of loans.

questions.question: ‘The Fall of a Sparrow’ is an autobiography of _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salim Ali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'The Fall of a Sparrow'** is an autobiography written by **Salim Ali**.
 
• Salim Ali is renowned as the **"Birdman of India"** for his significant contributions to ornithology.
 
• The book provides a detailed account of his life, his work in the field of bird study, and his experiences.
 
• Salim Ali's work has been instrumental in the establishment of ornithology as a scientific discipline in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Salim Ali was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in 1958 and the **Padma Vibhushan** in 1976, which are among India's highest civilian honors.
 
• He played a crucial role in the establishment of the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) and the Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary.
 
• His extensive fieldwork and publications have greatly enhanced the understanding and conservation of birds in India.
